clinician.final_diagnosis: Scleredema type 2 associated with IgA-κ smoldering myeloma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 66-year-old Sri Lankan woman with a 34-year history of skin disease initially diagnosed as diffuse systemic sclerosis presented with acute exacerbation of widespread skin thickening predominantly involving the trunk and proximal extremities. Clinical examination showed absence of sclerodactyly and Raynaud's phenomenon, with negative autoimmune antibody profile and normal systemic investigations (blood counts, biochemistry, echocardiography, chest imaging, and upper GI endoscopy). Skin biopsy from four body sites revealed scleredema histopathology (normal epidermis, thickened reticular dermis with fenestrated collagen bundles separated by clear spaces, non-atrophied skin appendages, and Alcian blue-positive interstitial mucin deposition), which prompted investigation for underlying plasma cell dyscrasia. Serum protein electrophoresis demonstrated an abnormal monoclonal band in the gamma region with paraprotein level of 8.9 g/dl. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed plasma cell dyscrasia with 15% abnormal monoclonal plasma cells showing multinuclearity. Staging workup showed no end organ damage (normal calcium, renal function, full blood count) and no bone involvement on whole-body MRI, meeting criteria for smoldering myeloma. The diagnosis was revised from systemic sclerosis to scleredema type 2 associated with IgA-κ smoldering myeloma. Treatment was initiated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) monthly (1 g/kg for 2 days per month) and intravenous bortezomib cycles (1.7 g on days 1, 8, 22, and 29). After 6 months of IVIG and four cycles of bortezomib, significant improvement of skin manifestations was observed.
